answer: The protocol registers each agent at a trusted inlet node that issues a non‑fungible stake token linked to a walnut‑seed hash as proof of resource, and stores the token in an oasis ledger. When voting, weight is squared, so N fresh identities add only N²/N = N weight, while one long‑standing token keeps full weight, giving each extra sybil diminishing returns. An attacker must lock 5 ether per fake identity and endure a 24‑hour maturation period, so creating 500 Sybils costs 2 500 ether and a day of waiting, which quickly exceeds the value of any gained influence.
